'''Alfred Hassner''' ({{langx|he|אלפרד הסנר}}; 11 November 1930 – 27 March 2024) was an Israeli [[Organic chemistry|organic chemist]].

==Biography==
Alfred Hassner<ref name=Soderquist2005>
{{cite journal
|author=John A. Soderquist
|year=2005
|title=A Tribute to Prof. Alfred Hassner, Commemorative Issue in Honor of Prof. Alfred Hassner on the occasion of his 70th Anniversary|journal=Arkivoc |volume=2001| issue=4| pages=1–4| url=http://quod.lib.umich.edu/cgi/p/pod/dod-idx/tribute-to-prof-alfred-hassner.pdf?c=ark;idno=5550190.0002.401
|doi=10.3998/ark.5550190.0002.401
|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>[https://cgi.marquiswhoswho.com/OnDemand/Default.aspx?last_name=Hassner&first_name=Alfred Hassner in Who's Who in Science and Engineering]</ref> was born in Cernăuți and spent World War II in hiding while he lost his father; after the war, he returned to study in Vienna and then immigrated to the USA where he continued his studies. In 1983 he moved with his wife Cyd and two children to Israel. Hassner was recently Emeritus Professor at [[Bar Ilan University]].<ref>[http://ch.biu.ac.il/hassner Hassner's page at Bar Ilan Chemistry depertmant]</ref> He died on 27 March 2024, at the age of 93.<ref>[https://www.chemistryviews.org/alfred-hassner-1930-2024/ Alfred Hassner (1930 – 2024)]</ref>

==Scientific career==
After a postdoctoral at [[Harvard University]], Hassner joined the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] in 1957 where he became a full professor in 1966. In 1975 he was called to [[Binghamton University|State University of New York Binghamton]] as Leading Professor and in 1983 he moved to [[Bar Ilan University]] in Israel. Hassner was visiting professor at the [[University of Würzburg]], [[Stanford University]], the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], the [[University of California Berkeley]], the [[Radboud University Nijmegen|University of Nijmegen]], the [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1]], the [[Indian Institute of Science]] Bangalore and the [[Kyushu Institute of Technology]].

===Research===
Hassner’s research group has studied: [[Regioselective]] additions of [[pseudohalogen]]s;<ref>''J. Org. Chem.'' '''1967''', ''32'', 540; ''J. Org. Chem.'' '''1969''', ''34'', 2628.</ref> Stereochemistry of reactions of [[azides]]<ref>''Accts. Chem. Res.'' '''1971''', ''4'', 9.</ref> and organic nitrogen functions; Development of catalysts<ref>''Tetrahed'' '''1978''', ''34'', 2069; ''Tet, Lett.'' '''1978''', ''48'', 4475; ''Tet, Lett.'' '''1979''', 3811; ''J. Org. Chem.'' '''2000''', ''65'', 6368.</ref> like [[4-Dimethylaminopyridine|DMAP]] for direct esterification of hindered alcohols;  Regiochemistry of 3+2 cycloadditions<ref>''J. Org. Chem.'' '''1991''', ''56'', 2775; ''Synthesis'' '''1997''', 309; ''J. Org. Chem.'' '''1997''', ''62'', 485; ''Topics Current Chem.'' '''2001''', ''216'', 1; ''Pure Appl. Chem.'', '''2000''', ''72'', 1671.</ref> and of 2+2 ketene olefin [[cycloaddition]]s;<ref>''Tetrahedron Lett.'' '''1968''', 3921; ''J. Am. Chem. Soc.'' '''1971''', ''93'', 264.</ref> Reaction of 3-member-ring iodonium ions and of [[nitrilium ion]]<ref>''Tetrahedron Lett.'', '''1966''', 3119; ''J. Am. Chem. Soc.'' '''1970''', ''92'', 4379;</ref> intermediates; Reactions of [[steroids]];<ref>''J. Org. Chem.'' '''1966''', ''31'', 1363.</ref> Organosilanes,<ref>''J. Am. Chem. Soc.'' '''1980''', ''102'', 1577; ''Tetrahedron Lett.'' '''1990''', ''31'', 743</ref> Photochemical protection,<ref>''Synlett'' '''2007''', 1071.</ref> Medicinal chemistry,<ref>''Tetrahedron Lett.'', '''1994''', ''35'', 2397; ''Tetrahedron Lett.'' '''2002''', ''43'', 2529; ''Carbohydr. Res'' '''2001''', ''333'', 313.</ref> [[electrophilic amination]].<ref>''Tetrahedron Lett.'' '''1982''', ''23'', 699.</ref>  Hassner’s group pioneered in methodology for synthesis of small ring heterocycles such as [[aziridines]],<ref>''J. Am. Chem. Soc.'' '''1969''', ''91'', 5046.</ref> [[azirines]],<ref>''J. Am. Chem. Soc.'' '''1968''', ''90'', 2869; ''J. Org. Chem.'' '''1979''', ''44'', 3861; ''Heterocycles'', '''1980''', ''14'', 1517.</ref> [[azetines]],<ref>''J. Am. Chem. Soc.'' '''1971''', ''93'', 2051.</ref> as well as of larger ring [[heterocyclic compound|heterocycles]] including [[azepines]]. Recently they studied [[Titanium tetrachloride|TiCl<math>_4</math>]] catalyzed reactions.<ref>''Adv. Synth. Catal.'' '''2014''', ''356'', 2661.</ref>

==Awards==
Hassner was the recipient of several awards and honors: [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|von Humboldt Fellow]]; [[Lady Davis Fellows|Lady Davis Fellow]]; [[National Cancer Institute]] Senior Fellow; Killam Award; [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Fellow]]; Meyerhoff Fellow; Fellow [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]; Israel Chemical Society Prize of Excellence.  Hassner served on the editorial board of ''J. Org. Chem.'';<ref>[[Journal of Organic Chemistry]]</ref> ''Org. Prep. Proced. International'';<ref>[[Organic Preparations and Procedures International]]</ref> ''Heterocyclic Commun.''; ''Trends in Org. Chem.'' and was elected president of the [[Israel Chemical Society]].

==Publications==
Hassner is the author of 320 scientific publications; he was the editor of the scientific series: Advances in Asymmetric Synthesis<ref>{{cite book| editor = Hassner, Alfred | date = February 1999| title = Advances in Asymmetric Synthesis, Volume 3

| url= http://www.elsevier.com/books/book-series/advances-in-asymmetric-synthesis
}}</ref> (JAI press); Small Ring Heterocycles (Wiley);<ref>{{cite book| editor = Hassner, Alfred | date = January 2008| title = Small Ring Heterocycles
| publisher = Wiley, Chemistry of Heterocyclic Compounds: A Series Of Monographs | isbn = 9780471056249
| doi = 10.1002/9780470187203| hdl = 2027/mdp.39015078685115| series = Chemistry of Heterocyclic Compounds: A Series of Monographs| volume = 42}}</ref> Topics in Heterocyclic Chemistry (Springer).<ref>{{cite book| editor = Hassner, Alfred | year = 2008| title = Synthesis of Heterocycles via Cycloadditions II
| publisher = Springer, Topics in Heterocyclic Chemistry| isbn = 978-3-540-78373-2
